feature: Every gap in a stack is the gap you typed
summary: A piece that changes size on its way into a stack no longer leaves the gap after it short. A label that re-wraps, or a whole stack that re-flows, when it is stretched across a column now settles before anything is placed, so the piece under it sits the gap you typed below it while you are dragging, not only after you let go.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on: this is how stacks lay out now.

try.do: New blank canvas. Draw a small square, and under it a text box saying a sentence long enough to wrap.
Select both, press Command G, then press Stack in the Layout section.
Draw one square above that group and one below it.
Select all three, press Command G, press Stack again.
In Layout, set Width to Fixed and type 300.
Under Contents of, set Horizontal to Stretch. The inner stack narrows to 300 and its words wrap onto more lines.
Drag the group's right edge further in and WATCH the bottom square while the button is still down.
Drop a Card from the Library and read the space above and below its title.

evaluate: While you drag the edge, does the bottom square keep an even distance under the words, or does it swim?
Does the spacing you see mid drag match what you get when you let go?
On the Card, does the title look equally spaced from the picture above it and the line below it?
Is a stack inside a stack something you would actually build this way, or did the steps above feel like a trick?
rough: I could not reproduce the reported one point gap on the Card. Measured with both the app's real text measurement and the model's own, the settled Card has exactly 8 above and 8 below its title, before and after this change. What IS real is the mechanism the report named: a piece that changes size as it is placed. It shows during a live drag, where a group is laid out once: the square under the inner stack used to sit 28 points too high, exactly the wrapped line the stack had just gained.

The before and after pictures are both here: 2026-09-06-even-gaps-mid-drag-before-sc.png and 2026-09-06-even-gaps-mid-drag-sc.png, same walk, same moment, the only difference being this fix. Screen Recording was granted, so both are real captures of the window.

The document level reflow was hiding this after the fact by running the whole layout again, so a settled document already looked right. That is why the fix is also faster: reflowing a document whose stacks hold pieces that re-fit went from 5.5ms to 4.0ms, since the pass it no longer needs costs more than the asking does. A document where nothing re-fits pays about 11 percent more inside its one pass.

The flow gives up after three rounds of asking. A piece that can never take the size it is given, like words with a single word too long for the room, keeps its overhang and the last answer stands, which is what it did before.
